name: Lunar distance check
values: Earth-Moon distance (km)=Moon.dist_from_earth_km|One-way radio delay from Earth (s)=Moon.light_time_from_earth_s
why_nasa_cares: Knowing exactly where the Moon is lets a crew aim for it, and a 1.4 second radio delay means Earth can still talk to the ship almost live.

name: Deep Space Network link
values: DSN ground complexes=dsn_complexes.number|Largest dish at each site (m)=dsn_70m.number|Other dishes at each site (m)=dsn_34m.number
why_nasa_cares: Every deep-space craft sends its data home through these three sites; as Earth turns, the next site picks up the signal so contact is never lost.

name: Voyager 1 marker
values: Voyager 1 mass (kg)=v1_mass.value|Power from each of 3 RTGs at launch (W)=v1_rtg_power.value
why_nasa_cares: Voyager 1 is a light, low-power craft that still talks to Earth from the edge of the Solar System: proof that a small ship can do big science.

name: TRAPPIST-1 e beacon
values: Radius (Earth = 1)=TRAPPIST-1 e.radius_earth|Starlight received (Earth = 1)=TRAPPIST-1 e.insolation_earth|Equilibrium temperature (K)=TRAPPIST-1 e.eq_temp_k|Distance (parsec)=TRAPPIST-1 e.distance_pc
why_nasa_cares: An Earth-sized planet that gets a bit less light than Earth is the kind of world NASA studies when it looks for places that could support life.
